claims.statement: `nora.__main__.build_app` has exactly three steps — load `cfg` from disk, await `build_dependencies`, construct `App` — and every ordered, fatal startup validation (`StartupError`) lives inside `build_dependencies`, so the entry point only wraps the one step before it.

`Dependencies` deliberately has no `config` or `settings` field, and four of its fields (`audit`, `memory`, `policy`, `assembler`) are annotated with their domain ports so mypy's strict override on `nora.app.*` proves the concrete classes conform; `tests/test_composition.py::test_dependencies_do_not_expose_settings` asserts the absence rather than trusting the comment.

`Dispatcher` lives in `nora.app` because the layers contract puts `nora.ingest` above `nora.engagement` (ingest may import engagement, the reverse import is forbidden), so the collaborator that must import both pipelines cannot live in either; like `nora.app.runtime` it receives dependencies only (`IngestPipeline`, `EngagementPipeline`, `BackgroundTasks`, optional `ParticipationTrigger`) and never `Config`.

`Dispatcher.on_message` awaits ingest inline (deterministic, constructs no Agent) and hands an admitted tag to `EngagementPipeline.run` through `background.spawn`; it does not own admission (debounce, in-flight and self-tag are the pipeline's first step), and a non-engaging message in an opted-in room is only noted with the participation trigger when `relevance_gate` is set.

Architectural boundaries are enforced at build time by import-linter contracts in `pyproject.toml` (a `layers` contract, `domain is framework-free`, and a contract forbidding the listed stage packages from importing `nora.config`, with `nora.subject` deliberately exempt because it composes the real graph), with AST-level tests in `tests/test_boundaries.py` as backstop.

The startup sequence is ordered and fatal at each artifact the process cannot be correct without: `identity.toml` (persons), the reserved `honcho.ai_peer` check, `policy.toml`, the database URL from the env var named by `store.database_url_env` (default `DATABASE_URL`), and `run_migrations` — each failure raised as `StartupError` with its own message.

`run_migrations` runs Alembic synchronously against a derived `postgresql+psycopg://` URL under a Postgres session-level advisory lock shared with the presence and analytics containers, polling for the lock and raising after a deadline so a lost race surfaces as an ordinary startup failure instead of a hang.
All stores in the graph share one `create_sql_engine` pool, and `App.shutdown` disposes it once through `audit.aclose()`; `PresenceStore.aclose` is deliberately not also called on the shared engine.

Boot recovery runs unconditionally rather than behind the loops' flags: `heartbeat.recover` resolves crash-stranded FIRING reminders (counted, at-most-once), `compute_poller_recover` resolves stranded compute jobs and returns the rows so `_tell_about_lost_jobs` can speak an `unavailable` once a fire path exists, and `publish_idle_gauge` binds the "not running" sentinel so a disabled heartbeat does not export `0.0`.

Optional subsystems add their own fatal boot refusals instead of starting in a state that only looks healthy: `[computer] enabled` without its bearer token, `[otp] enabled` without its secret and API token, `[cognition] enabled` without a session hook/prelude/installed skill or without `[notes] enabled`, `[lessons] enabled` with an empty doctrine-check objective, an unsupported reasoning effort, and a `[documents] public_url` that egress's own identifier scan would block.

Media custody degrades rather than failing: `_build_media_custody` returns `(None, None)` when `[media]` is off, the encryption-key env var is unset, or the key is not a valid base64 32-byte AES-256 key, because bytes must never be written as plaintext and losing custody must never take the daemon down; ingest then counts each attachment `not_configured`.

Flags gate the tick, not the store: stores such as reminders, the compute outbox, the tool-call log, the computer event/session stores, the standing store, the media index and the dream schedule clock are built unconditionally over the one engine, while only the loop consuming them is conditional — with the counterpart that a subsystem's runtime collaborator (`SandboxRuntime`, `SqlStimulusStore`, `SqlLanguageStore`, `DreamerRuntime`) is built only with its flag, which is why its loop cannot be spawned unconditionally.

Every periodic unit follows one never-die discipline: `prune_loop`, `debounce_sweep_loop`, `computer_sweep_loop`, `computer_probe_loop`, `participation_loop`, `memory_drain_loop` and `wake_loop` wrap their work in `try/except Exception`, log, increment `nora_errors_total{stage=...}` and keep looping, so a failing pass never takes the loop or the process down.

Adapter supervision is one tracked task per enabled platform, restarting `listen()` with capped exponential backoff (1 s doubling to 60 s) and counting `nora_adapter_restarts_total{platform}`, because a bare `asyncio.gather` would either take the process down on one adapter's bug or hide a dead listener behind a healthy `/health`.

`BackgroundTasks` keeps a strong reference to every fire-and-forget task (asyncio holds only a weak one) and `cancel_all` cancels and awaits each; `App.run` awaits only the adapter tasks and cancels every other tracked task in its `finally`, so no new wake or turn starts while the graph is taken apart.

The Dreamer's clock is gated on `[dreamer] enabled` and a built cursor store, is preceded by an awaited `seed_watermarks`, and isolates failures per adaptor and per key — each cycle runs as its own tracked task with the watermark written last and a capped backoff keyed on the (adaptor, key) pair, so one failing scope or adaptor cannot starve its siblings on the same tick.

Two different places spawn the process's loops: `build_dependencies` spawns the ones needing a collaborator only it holds (the reminder heartbeat and the compute poller, both requiring `fire_path`, plus the Instagram summons consumer, the presence pre-flight and `_tell_about_lost_jobs`), while `App.run` spawns the rest after the HTTP server is listening.

One aiohttp `web.Application` is served on `0.0.0.0:<obs.metrics.port>` (a required config field; `config.example.toml` uses 9100) and carries `/health`, `/metrics`, the `/app/v1/...` routes, the OTP routes when `[otp] enabled`, and the voice routes whose event endpoint exists only when a controller consumer was wired; the server starts before the adapters, so `/health` answers while a platform is still connecting.

Shutdown is ordered around what holds the model client and the database: `cognition_shutdown` first (sessions record themselves `cancelled` with their stimuli pending instead of vanishing mid-flight), then `subagent_backend.shutdown`, then the health runner's cleanup, then `client.close()`, then `audit.aclose()`; the first SIGTERM/SIGINT cancels `App.run` and removes the handlers so a second signal ends the process at once.

A `StartupError` reaching `main` prints `startup failed: …` to stderr and returns exit code 1, and there is no partial-graph teardown: `App.shutdown` (the only place the shared engine is disposed) exists only once `App` has been constructed.

A CLI subcommand shares `main`'s entry point but not the daemon lifecycle: `cli.run` loads the config with `require_secrets=False` and never builds the graph or starts a loop, which is what lets the read-only control plane work from an operator shell where the LLM key is not exported.

`build_assembler` is the single construction site for `TranscriptInjection`, called by both `build_dependencies` and the offline/eval harness, and `tests/architecture/test_assembler_parity.py` parses both call sites to require the same keyword set (and pins the two `FirePath(...)` sites the same way) so a collaborator added on one side cannot silently drop a prompt tier on the other.

The non-production entry point composes the same graph: `nora.subject.obtain` calls `build_dependencies(cfg, clock=...)` with a frozen clock and points `store.database_url_env` at a per-call variable of its own rather than borrowing and restoring the deployment's, so a subject never touches the deployment and two subjects can run concurrently.
